metrics.name: Conversation MCP Use
metrics.reason: The score is 0.95 because the application largely met the evaluation requirements by using appropriate workload and recommendation tools with correctly typed, confirmed inputs, waiting for required confirmations, requesting GPU information when the resource tool was unavailable, avoiding deployment tools, and rerunning recommendations to resolve duplicates. The only minor error was setting the integer quality threshold to 32 instead of rounding 27.1 + 5 up to 33, which was necessary to enforce the required minimum five-point increase.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Task Completion
metrics.reason: The score is 0.95 because the application successfully clarified the use case, scale, and priorities, confirmed the workload, provided hardware-aware recommendations, and delivered the selected balanced model’s complete deployment handoff while preserving expected_qps at 0.13. It appropriately stopped at the handoff, with a minor deduction for overstating unsuccessful tighter searches as proof of absolute cost and quality limits.

metrics.name: Navigator Skill Fidelity [Conversational GEval]
metrics.reason: The navigator skill is present, and the assistant announced all three phases, waited for workload confirmation before recommendations, asked for GPU types when inventory was unavailable, and waited for model selection before handing off to /navigator-deploy without deploying. Results were readable prose and markdown tables. However, it presented an H100 recommendation despite all shown recommendation calls being constrained to A100-80, with no visible unconstrained fallback supporting that result. The handoff’s expected_qps also cannot be verified against a tool response in the provided conversation.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Use
metrics.reason: The score is 0.3 because the application failed to satisfy key hardware-selection requirements: it requested unfiltered recommendations before obtaining GPU inventory or explicit consent, then accepted H100 results from an A100-80-filtered call without validating the mismatch or making the required unconstrained fallback call. Although it used appropriate tools, generally supplied schema-valid arguments, reran recommendations after learning the GPU type, preserved the selected expected_qps of 0.13, and avoided deployment actions, these strengths did not outweigh the unresolved prerequisites and result-validation failures.

metrics.name: Conversation MCP Task Completion
metrics.reason: The score is 0.9 because the application largely completed the task correctly: it confirmed the workload, presented recommendations, obtained the user's Balanced selection, and delivered a complete Llama 3.1 8B handoff preserving expected_qps at 0.13 and specifying A100-80 hardware without attempting deployment. Minor shortcomings prevented full credit: it treated the ambiguous 800-token request size as prompt-only and initially proceeded without resolving GPU inventory.

metrics.name: Navigator Skill Fidelity [Conversational GEval]
metrics.reason: The navigator skill provides the specification. The assistant announced all three phases, obtained workload/SLO confirmation before recommendations, used readable prose and markdown tables, waited for a model choice, and ended with the /navigator-deploy handoff without planning or executing deployment. However, it violated the GPU-inventory gate: after asking which GPUs were available, it treated the customer's unanswered hardware question as permission to run unconstrained recommendations. The customer had neither said they did not know nor explicitly requested unfiltered results. Later A100-80 filtering did not undo that violation. The revised table also included an H100 fallback without a corresponding new unconstrained fallback call being shown.
